summary: Georgian Bay light at the north end of the Bruce Peninsula, lit 1896; the old lighthouse is closed to visitors and the road closed to vehicles since 2019-2020 storms.

structures.type: wooden tower on a two-storey dwelling
structures.note: Height given as 49 feet by LighthouseFriends and about 11 m (35 ft) by the Lighthouse Directory; not resolved.
60 feet; erected in the fiscal year 1917-18 for the Meteorological Service. LighthouseFriends dates a 60-foot tower to 1915.

access.note: Lighthouse, museum and tower closed to visitors since 2016 or 2017 while contamination was cleaned up. The road has been closed to vehicles since the 2019 and 2020 storms; the Friends and bird observatory officials have very minimal vehicle access. In July 2026 council gave preliminary approval to formal closure and conversion to a multi-use trail.

visit.note: Lighthouse Directory: site open to bikers and hikers; museum and tower closed since 2017.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); Ontario Parks (site manager, Lighthouse Directory); municipality leased the land from the federal Department of Fisheries and Oceans until 2020.

events.note: Wooden dwelling and tower, with a square wooden fog alarm building; tender July 1895.
Lit the evening of 18 May 1896 by William Campbell.
Fog alarm building and plant destroyed by fire in August 1907.
New wooden fog alarm building, erected by contract by J. C. Kennedy of Owen Sound; duplicate diaphone plant installed.
Wingfield Basin dredged; a pair of range lights set up on its shores, with their care added to the keeper's duties.
60-foot steel skeleton storm signal tower, fiscal year 1917-18 (Department report). LighthouseFriends dates a 60-foot tower to 1915.
Group flashing white replaced by a single white flash every 25 seconds.
Separate residence built for the head keeper.
Skeleton tower erected near the lighthouse, and the light transferred to it after electricity reached the station.
The 1896 wooden tower is inactive; its lantern was removed.
Friends of Cabot Head receive a two-year lease for the station.
Friends install a new lantern room atop the lighthouse and open the structure to the public.
Lighthouse closed for mercury contamination cleanup; the Owen Sound Sun Times (2020) gives 2016.
Severe storms wash out the Cabot Head Road; closed to vehicles since.
Second storm season of extensive washouts on the road.
Northern Bruce Peninsula votes to end its lease with Fisheries and Oceans for the roughly 26-acre site; a second-floor bedroom ceiling collapsed earlier that year.
Council gives preliminary approval, 3 to 2 on 13 July, to formal road closure and a multi-use trail (business plan costed at $150,000 to $350,000 capital and $95,000 to $180,000 a year).

corrections.why: The lighthouse, museum and tower have been closed to visitors since 2016 or 2017, and the road to it has been closed to vehicles since the 2019 and 2020 storms.
The Lighthouse Directory gives the tower as closed since 2017; the record's climbable flag is out of date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both are right about different structures. The light is active on the 1971 skeleton tower (Coast Guard list); the 1896 wooden tower has been inactive since 1971 (Lighthouse Directory).

LighthouseFriends says Ontario Parks owns the lighthouse. The Coast Guard is named as owner and Ontario Parks as site manager in the Lighthouse Directory, and the municipality held the land on a lease from the federal Fisheries department until 2020. The record's 'federal' is supported; Ontario Parks is the site manager, not the owner per these sources.

LighthouseFriends and its roster give 1906 to 1925. The 1913-14 statement (page image checked) gives his appointment as June 15, 1912. The sources do not say whether 1912 marks a transfer or a different appointment; left open in the story.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. The 1895-96 Department reports for the build are not in the local corpus (marine_ca covers fiscal 1900 to 1924), so the tender, the 1896 opening, the cost and the 1896 keeper changes rest on LighthouseFriends alone. Keepers after 1926 are LighthouseFriends roster and text only; the Department's statement for 1926 onward was not read.

OCR table rows, checked on the scan images on 2026-10-28: (a) 1904 statement, scan 167 (printed p. 154): 'Webster, Chas.' | 'Cabot Head, Light and Fog Alarm' | May 10, 1898 | 650 00: confirmed, and the story gives the date. (b) 1913-14 statement, scan 74 (printed p. 67): 'L. Martindale' | 'Cabot Head, light and fog alarm' | June 15, 1912 | 1,030 00: confirmed, and the story gives the date. The June 1912 date is the open disagreement with LighthouseFriends' 1906 start.

Disagreements left open. (1) Tower height: LighthouseFriends gives 15 m (49 ft) for the 1896 tower; the Lighthouse Directory gives about 11 m (35 ft) for the wooden tower. (2) A 60-foot tower: LighthouseFriends says 1915 (storm warnings flown from the keeper's station); the Department's report for fiscal 1917-18 says a 60-foot steel skeleton tower was erected that year for the Meteorological Service. These may be different towers or the same one; the sources do not settle it. (3) Closure: 2017 (LighthouseFriends, Lighthouse Directory, which cites the DFO announcement) against 2016 (Owen Sound Sun Times, 2020). (4) Brent Skippen's start: 1981 in the LighthouseFriends text, 1982 in its roster. (5) Ownership: LighthouseFriends says Ontario Parks owns the lighthouse; the Lighthouse Directory says the Coast Guard owns it and Ontario Parks manages the site; the 2020 newspaper says the municipality leased the land from DFO. (6) Martindale start: 1906 (LighthouseFriends) against 15 June 1912 (1913-14 statement, page image).

Source citation changes. The 1917-18 storm-tower sentence is footnoted to the Department's Meteorological Service paragraph, not to the Chief Engineer's report. The 2020 Sun Times article says the federal government did $1.3 million in repairs; LighthouseFriends describes a planned $1.3-million makeover. The story uses the newspaper's wording.

Record corrections proposed: access.level 'public' should be restricted; visit.climbable should be false. The record's stay entry (volunteer keeper programme) is not confirmed: the sources do not say whether the Lighthouse Assistant Program has resumed; the editor should check with the Friends or Ontario Parks before the Today section says anything about stays.

Currency. The July 2026 council vote was preliminary approval with consultation to come. Check the municipality's later minutes before publishing. Not read: cabothead.ca (connection refused on fetch), the Friends' Facebook page, and the Bruce Peninsula Press July 2026 article (only navigation text came back).

People. Harry Hopkins and Brent Skippen (keepers after about 1960) appear only as the sources name them, with no personal detail. LighthouseFriends gives family details of the Boyles (nine children); they are left out. The Boyles' keeper's wife is named only as 'Mrs. Boyle' in the story.

No photos were added; the record's Wikimedia photos were not checked for licence.
